passages.text: What causes conflicts and quarrels among you? Don’t they come from the passions at war within you?
passages.original: Πόθεν πόλεμοι καὶ πόθεν μάχαι ἐν ὑμῖν οὐκ ἐντεῦθεν ἐκ τῶν ἡδονῶν ὑμῶν τῶν στρατευομένων ἐν τοῖς μέλεσιν ὑμῶν
passages.objections:
It's always someone else's fault when we argue; I never do anything wrong.
If people would just listen to me, we wouldn't have any fights.
All our problems come from outside forces, not from anything inside us.
I can't help it if I get angry—it's just the way things are.
Quarrels happen because others are jealous of me, not because of anything I want.
There's nothing wrong with following my desires; they don't cause any trouble.
If everyone just got what they wanted, there would be no conflicts.
Arguments are just bad luck, not something we can control.
My feelings and wants have nothing to do with the fights I get into.
It's impossible for our own desires to cause any real problems between us.

passages.text: You crave what you do not have; you kill and covet, but are unable to obtain it. You quarrel and fight. You do not have, because you do not ask.
passages.original: ἐπιθυμεῖτε καὶ οὐκ ἔχετε φονεύετε καὶ ζηλοῦτε καὶ οὐ δύνασθε ἐπιτυχεῖν μάχεσθε καὶ πολεμεῖτε οὐκ ἔχετε διὰ τὸ μὴ αἰτεῖσθαι ὑμᾶς
passages.objections:
If I just want something badly enough, I’ll eventually get it, no matter what.
Fighting and competing with others is the only way to get ahead in life.
If I take what I want from others, I’ll finally be satisfied.
It’s pointless to ask for help; I have to do everything myself.
If I envy what others have, it will motivate me to succeed.
Hurting others is justified if it means I get what I desire.
I never get what I want because the world is just unfair to me.
If I’m aggressive enough, I’ll always come out on top.
There’s no use in asking for anything—I’ll never receive it anyway.
Coveting what others have is just a normal part of life; there’s nothing wrong with it.

passages.text: And when you do ask, you do not receive, because you ask with wrong motives, that you may squander it on your pleasures.
passages.original: αἰτεῖτε καὶ οὐ λαμβάνετε διότι κακῶς αἰτεῖσθε ἵνα ἐν ταῖς ἡδοναῖς ὑμῶν δαπανήσητε
passages.objections:
I keep praying for more money, but God never listens to me.
If I want something really badly, God should just give it to me, right?
Why bother asking God for things if He never gives me what I want?
I don’t see why my reasons for asking matter—shouldn’t God just answer my prayers anyway?
It’s not fair that God doesn’t give me what I ask for, even if it’s just for my own enjoyment.
I thought God was supposed to give us whatever we desire if we pray hard enough.
If I pray for something selfish, God should still grant it because He loves me.
I don’t think my motives have anything to do with whether my prayers are answered.
Why would God care if I use His blessings just for myself?
If I ask for something to make my life easier, that should be enough reason for God to say yes.

passages.text: You adulteresses! Do you not know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Therefore, whoever chooses to be a friend of the world renders himself an enemy of God.
passages.original: Μοιχαλίδες οὐκ οἴδατε ὅτι ἡ φιλία τοῦ κόσμου ἔχθρα τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν οὖν βουληθῇ φίλος εἶναι τοῦ κόσμου ἐχθρὸς τοῦ Θεοῦ καθίσταται
passages.objections:
I don’t see any harm in getting along with everyone and fitting in with the world.
Why can’t I just enjoy what everyone else does and still be close to God?
Isn’t it possible to love God and still follow the world’s ways?
I think I can be friends with everyone, no matter what they believe or do.
Why would God care if I just want to be accepted by people around me?
I don’t think there’s anything wrong with chasing after what the world offers.
Can’t I just blend in and not make a big deal about my faith?
I don’t see why I have to choose between God and the world.
Isn’t it better to be popular and well-liked, even if it means compromising a little?
I don’t think being friends with the world makes me an enemy of God.

passages.text: Or do you think the Scripture says without reason that the Spirit He caused to dwell in us yearns with envy?
passages.original: ἢ δοκεῖτε ὅτι κενῶς ἡ γραφὴ λέγει Πρὸς φθόνον ἐπιποθεῖ τὸ πνεῦμα ὃ κατῴκισεν ἐν ἡμῖν
passages.objections:
I don’t think the Scriptures really mean anything when they talk about the Spirit’s desires.
Maybe those old writings are just poetic and not meant to be taken seriously.
I doubt God actually cares about what’s going on inside us.
The Spirit probably doesn’t have any strong feelings about how we live.
I’m sure those verses are just empty words, not meant for us today.
Why would God’s Spirit care if I follow my own path?
I don’t see why the Scriptures would warn us if it wasn’t just a figure of speech.
It’s not like the Spirit is actually jealous or concerned about our loyalty.
Those warnings in Scripture are probably just for dramatic effect, not real guidance.

passages.text: But He gives us more grace. This is why it says: “God opposes the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
passages.original: μείζονα δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν διὸ λέγει Ὁ Θεὸς ὑπερηφάνοις ἀντιτάσσεται ταπεινοῖς δὲ δίδωσιν χάριν
passages.objections:
I don’t see why I should humble myself—being proud is what gets you ahead in life.
If I act like I’m better than everyone else, surely God will be impressed by my confidence.
Why would God care if I’m proud? Isn’t self-importance a sign of strength?
I don’t need anyone’s help, not even God’s—I can do everything on my own.
Only the weak need to be humble; I’d rather stand tall and show off my achievements.
If I admit my faults and lower myself, people will just walk all over me.
God must favor those who are bold and assertive, not those who are meek and lowly.
Why should I bother being humble when pride makes me feel powerful?
I don’t think God pays attention to attitudes—He only cares about what I do, not how I think about myself.

passages.text: Submit yourselves, then, to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.
passages.original: Ὑποτάγητε οὖν τῷ Θεῷ ἀντίστητε δὲ τῷ διαβόλῳ καὶ φεύξεται ἀφ’ ὑμῶν
passages.objections:
I don’t think I have any power to stand up to evil; it’s just too strong for me.
Why should I bother resisting temptation? It never seems to make a difference.
If I try to fight against the devil, won’t he just keep coming back stronger?
God doesn’t really care if I give in to sin now and then, does He?
I feel like I’m on my own when it comes to spiritual battles.
There’s no point in submitting to God; nothing in my life ever changes.
Evil is everywhere, so it’s impossible to escape its influence.
I’m too weak to resist; I might as well just give up.
If I try to get closer to God, I’ll just end up failing again.
I don’t think the devil is really interested in someone like me.

passages.text: Draw near to God, and He will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners, and purify your hearts, you double-minded.
passages.original: ἐγγίσατε τῷ Θεῷ καὶ ἐγγιεῖ ὑμῖν καθαρίσατε χεῖρας ἁμαρτωλοί καὶ ἁγνίσατε καρδίας δίψυχοι
passages.objections:
I don’t think God wants anything to do with people like me after all I’ve done.
It’s impossible to get close to God; He’s too far away and doesn’t care about us.
Why bother trying to change? My past mistakes can’t be washed away.
God only listens to holy people, not someone who keeps messing up like me.
I can’t approach God until I’ve fixed every part of my life first.
There’s no point in praying—God won’t respond to someone as double-minded as I am.
I’m too sinful to ever be accepted by God, so why even try?
God doesn’t want us to come to Him; He’s just waiting to judge us.
If I just keep living the way I am, maybe things will work out without needing to change.
It’s not possible to really change my heart or my actions, so I might as well give up.

passages.text: Grieve, mourn, and weep. Turn your laughter to mourning, and your joy to gloom.
passages.original: ταλαιπωρήσατε καὶ πενθήσατε καὶ κλαύσατε ὁ γέλως ὑμῶν εἰς πένθος μετατραπήτω καὶ ἡ χαρὰ εἰς κατήφειαν
passages.objections:
Why should I feel bad about anything I’ve done? I’m just trying to enjoy my life.
I don’t see the point in being sad or mourning—shouldn’t we always be happy?
If I just ignore my mistakes and keep smiling, everything will work out fine.
There’s no need to take my sins seriously; everyone messes up sometimes.
Why should I stop celebrating and start feeling guilty?
I don’t think feeling sorrowful helps anyone; it just makes things worse.
Isn’t it better to laugh off our problems instead of dwelling on them?
I don’t need to change my attitude—joy is all that matters.
Why should I let my happiness be interrupted by regret or grief?
If I’m having fun, why should I let anything bring me down?

passages.text: Humble yourselves before the Lord, and He will exalt you.
passages.original: ταπεινώθητε ἐνώπιον Κυρίου καὶ ὑψώσει ὑμᾶς
passages.objections:
Why should I lower myself before anyone? I deserve to be recognized for my own achievements.
I don’t see the point in being humble; people just walk all over you if you do that.
If I want to get ahead, I have to promote myself and make sure everyone knows how great I am.
No one else is going to lift me up, so I have to do it myself.
Humility is for the weak; strong people take what they want.
If I admit my faults, people will think less of me.
Why should I care what God thinks about my attitude?
I’ve worked hard for everything I have, so I deserve to be proud.
If I don’t boast about my successes, no one will notice me.
Being humble just means letting others take credit for what I’ve done.

passages.text: Brothers, do not slander one another. Anyone who speaks against his brother or judges him speaks against the law and judges it. And if you judge the law, you are not a practitioner of the law, but a judge of it.
passages.original: Μὴ καταλαλεῖτε ἀλλήλων ἀδελφοί ὁ καταλαλῶν ἀδελφοῦ ἢ κρίνων τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ καταλαλεῖ νόμου καὶ κρίνει νόμον εἰ δὲ νόμον κρίνεις οὐκ εἶ ποιητὴς νόμου ἀλλὰ κριτής
passages.objections:
I have every right to talk badly about others if they’ve wronged me.
If someone messes up, it’s my duty to point it out to everyone.
I’m just being honest when I criticize my brother; it’s not slander.
If I don’t judge others, how will they ever learn from their mistakes?
It’s not a big deal to gossip a little about people in the church.
I follow the law better than most, so I can judge those who don’t.
Calling out someone’s faults publicly is the only way to keep the community pure.
If I don’t speak against my brother, I’m letting sin go unchecked.
I’m not judging the law, just the people who break it.
It’s impossible to live together without talking about each other’s flaws.

passages.text: There is only one Lawgiver and Judge, the One who is able to save and destroy. But who are you to judge your neighbor?
passages.original: εἷς ἐστιν ὁ νομοθέτης καὶ κριτής ὁ δυνάμενος σῶσαι καὶ ἀπολέσαι σὺ δὲ τίς εἶ ὁ κρίνων τὸν πλησίον
passages.objections:
I think it’s my job to decide who’s worthy and who isn’t around here.
If someone messes up, I have every right to condemn them.
I know better than most people, so I should be the one to judge their actions.
It’s up to me to make sure others get what they deserve.
I can tell who’s good and who’s bad just by looking at them.
If I don’t judge my neighbor, who will keep them in line?
I’m sure I understand the law well enough to pass judgment on others.
Some people just need to be put in their place, and I’m the one to do it.
I don’t see why I shouldn’t decide who’s right or wrong among us.
It’s not enough to follow the rules myself—I have to enforce them on everyone else too.

passages.text: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, spend a year there, carry on business, and make a profit.”
passages.original: Ἄγε νῦν οἱ λέγοντες Σήμερον ἢ αὔριον πορευσόμεθα εἰς τήνδε τὴν πόλιν καὶ ποιήσομεν ἐκεῖ ἐνιαυτὸν καὶ ἐμπορευσόμεθα καὶ κερδήσομεν
passages.objections:
I already know exactly what will happen tomorrow, so I don’t need to worry about anything.
I’m in control of my own future, and nothing can stop my plans.
If I work hard enough, I can guarantee my success next year.
There’s no need to consider anything but my own goals when making plans.
I can decide where I’ll go and what I’ll do without thinking about anyone else.
My business will definitely succeed because I’ve planned everything perfectly.
I don’t need to ask for guidance; I know what’s best for me.
Nothing unexpected ever happens, so I can be sure of my profits.
I don’t need to rely on anyone else when it comes to my future.
I can boast about my plans because I’m certain they’ll work out just as I want.

passages.text: You do not even know what will happen tomorrow! What is your life? You are a mist that appears for a little while and then vanishes.
passages.original: οἵτινες οὐκ ἐπίστασθε τὸ τῆς αὔριον ποία ἡ ζωὴ ὑμῶν ἀτμὶς γάρ ἐστε ἡ πρὸς ὀλίγον φαινομένη ἔπειτα καὶ ἀφανιζομένη
passages.objections:
I know exactly what my future holds, nothing can surprise me.
My plans for tomorrow are set in stone, nothing will change them.
Life goes on forever, so I don’t need to worry about what comes next.
I have plenty of time to do whatever I want, there’s no rush.
I’m in complete control of my destiny, nothing is uncertain.
Tomorrow is guaranteed, so I can put things off as long as I like.
I don’t need to think about how short life is, there’s always another day.
Nothing unexpected ever happens to me, so I don’t need to be cautious.
I can make promises about the future because I know I’ll be here.
My life is solid and lasting, not fragile or temporary.

passages.text: Instead, you ought to say, “If the Lord is willing, we will live and do this or that.”
passages.original: Ἀντὶ τοῦ λέγειν ὑμᾶς Ἐὰν ὁ Κύριος θελήσῃ καὶ ζήσομεν καὶ ποιήσομεν τοῦτο ἢ ἐκεῖνο
passages.objections:
I don’t need to ask anyone’s permission for my plans—my future is in my own hands.
Why should I bother thinking about what God wants? I already know what’s best for me.
I can guarantee my own success if I just work hard enough.
There’s no point in considering God’s will; He doesn’t care about my daily choices.
I’m sure nothing unexpected will happen—I’ve got everything under control.
I don’t need to rely on anyone else, not even God, to make my plans work.
If I want something, I just have to go out and get it—no need to wait for anyone’s approval.
My plans are set, and nothing can change them.
I don’t see why I should leave room for uncertainty when I’m so confident in my abilities.
God doesn’t get involved in business or travel plans; that’s all up to me.

passages.text: As it is, you boast in your proud intentions. All such boasting is evil.
passages.original: νῦν δὲ καυχᾶσθε ἐν ταῖς ἀλαζονείαις ὑμῶν πᾶσα καύχησις τοιαύτη πονηρά ἐστιν
passages.objections:
I don’t see anything wrong with bragging about my achievements—doesn’t it just show confidence?
If I don’t talk about my plans and successes, how will people know how capable I am?
It’s not a big deal to boast a little; everyone does it to get ahead.
Why shouldn’t I be proud of what I’ve accomplished on my own?
I think it’s fine to make bold claims about what I’ll do in the future.
Isn’t it harmless to show off my skills and make sure others notice?
If I don’t promote myself, who else will?
There’s nothing wrong with taking credit and making sure people know I’m the best.
I worked hard for what I have, so I deserve to boast about it.
Being proud and talking about my plans just motivates others to do better.

passages.text: Anyone, then, who knows the right thing to do, yet fails to do it, is guilty of sin.
passages.original: εἰδότι οὖν καλὸν ποιεῖν καὶ μὴ ποιοῦντι ἁμαρτία αὐτῷ ἐστιν
passages.objections:
I know what’s right, but as long as I don’t do anything wrong, I’m fine.
If I just avoid bad actions, it doesn’t matter if I ignore helping others.
It’s not a sin if I simply stay out of it and do nothing.
I can’t be held responsible for not getting involved when I see someone in need.
As long as I don’t break any rules, I’m not guilty of anything.
If I keep to myself and don’t interfere, I can’t be blamed for what happens.
It’s only a problem if I actually do something wrong, not if I just let things be.
I don’t have to act if it’s inconvenient, even if I know what’s right.
Not doing good isn’t the same as doing evil, so I shouldn’t worry about it.
